steps.content: Days of relentless rain have left the air humid and cold enough to chill the bones. Black shrouds, layered over the young dead, hide their faces.
Once the final body is laid to rest, a brief funeral commences within the curtain of falling rain.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: So foolish. They think breaking away from the metropoles means they're free. That they can now run their own industry, their own religion, and control their own resources. As if they can just farm and trade in peace in a world ravaged by catastrophes.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: But the world is a jungle, full of predators. When a weak lamb cries for independence and leaves the herd, it doesn't get freedom. It gets eaten.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: That's why... we have to stay on the right path. Even if our hand has to be iron. Even if it seems cruel. We must follow it, and guide them to follow it, too!
She casts her torch to the ground. In the flickering firelight that dances across their faces, the group moves as one—fists meeting chests in a solemn, silent salute, honoring the fallen soldiers.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: To all our brothers who lost their way!

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Your hate was used. Your pain was turned into a weapon against the city-state. But I still recognize you as one of us.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: I hope you find the prosperity and freedom you were looking for... here in your eternal rest.
You don't see Hilda among the crowd.
Having witnessed those truths, she can no longer bring herself to participate in a ceremony that so boldly champions the metropoles' agenda.
[Cellar]
(Footsteps)
You follow the trail of Mania deep into the cellar, your footsteps the only other sound in the oppressive quiet. At the far end, you find Hilda.
She is curled in the darkness, sitting before a telegraph machine. Her fingers dance across the keys in a slow, rhythmic cadence.
The dit-dah, dit-dah-dah fills the space like a sacred requiem.

Words feel like a desecration here. Instead, after a moment of shared silence, you lower yourself to the ground beside her. Remembering the code you devised yesterday, you begin to speak with your hands.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you doing?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Writing epitaphs for them.
Only now do you notice the stack of documents beside her. It's the guards' profiles.
With meticulous care, she transcribes each name, tapping them out into code. One by one, she transforms them into radio waves and releases them to the wind.
Perhaps the signals will be swallowed by Mania. Perhaps they will drift for years before any receiver finds them.
But... it doesn't matter. Someday, they will find their way home. To that place free of bloodshed and oppression.
You wait quietly beside her until the final name is sent. Then, she closes the telegraph machine, the quiet click a period at the end of her elegy.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...It couldn't have been easy to find this place.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I'm fine. I just wanted to stay in a quiet place for a while.
And to secretly mourn these "enemies," away from everyone else.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Here, I can hear voices from the past. When I need quiet, they keep me company.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Can you really hear them?
She leans in, her finger pressed to her lips. The earnest intensity in her eyes compels you. The world falls away as you still your breath and listen.
In the newfound silence, the darkness itself seems to breathe. And then you hear it—faint, indistinct voices, rising like a whisper from the void.

steps.speaker: Girl's Shadow
steps.content: Sis, look! The railway from the metropoles is almost here in the north. Soon you could see an art exhibition in the morning and be back with new books by afternoon.

steps.speaker: Man's Shadow
steps.content: Their engineers say we can redirect the underground springs to the dry regions. We'll finally be able to grow more food... feed more people in the satellite towns.

steps.speaker: Woman's Shadow
steps.content: Just think of how many children the medical program could save...

steps.speaker: Man's Shadow
steps.content: The united university is opening enrollment soon... More of our people will have a chance to study!

steps.speaker: Woman's Shadow
steps.content: Listen, everyone! This is our next goal. We're moving forward, one step at a time, toward the ideal city-state!

steps.speaker: Subtitles
steps.content: This is a crossroads for the world. In its street-side cafes, people peruse newspapers in dozens of languages, eagerly trading phrases from their homelands.

steps.speaker: Subtitles
steps.content: All children attend school; everyone has work and receives their rightful share. Theaters constantly debut new plays, and a laundry woman can walk proudly into a masquerade to dance with nobility.

steps.speaker: Subtitles
steps.content: No wars, no conflicts. People of every rank fulfill their duties, yet still have the energy to enjoy their lives.

steps.speaker: Subtitles
steps.content: Back then, it was the clearest vision of an ideal, an indestructible lighthouse in the hearts of countless souls.
...But what remains of it now?

steps.speaker: Shane's Shadow
steps.content: Why are you holding us back? Why are we the ones trapped here on the farm? Why are you stealing our future?

steps.speaker: Guard's Shadow
steps.content: Everyone who asked questions was taken... just disappeared. Where are they? Release them! Give them back!

steps.speaker: Girl's Shadow
steps.content: Why...? Why do we have to fight wars? Shouldn't we be working together? Shouldn't we be moving forward?
The silence is absolute, but her face is a transcript of a conversation you can't hear. An icy dread traces its way down your spine, and you can't stop yourself from asking.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What... do you hear?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: They ask me if I still remember what the ideal city-state was supposed to be. If I remember the person I used to be, the one who fought side by side with them for a shared future. They ask when the war will end... when the trees in our homeland will grow green again.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: They speak of everything... except the reason they died.

Her tone is deceptively calm, but you know better. These "voices from the past" are classic auditory hallucinations, a direct symptom of uncontrolled Mania that only emerges when a host's psyche is on the brink.

The cause could be physical—damage to the LINK—or purely psychological, with the unshackled Mania ravaging her mind. The origin matters less than the result: beneath her composed facade lies a profoundly fragile mental state.
She is just forcing normalcy, a performance as fragile as glass.
With a quiet sigh, you move to sit closer to her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This question has been tormenting you, hasn't it? Why has our city-state become what it is today?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And sometimes you wish it were you lying in that darkness instead of them.
You listen as Hilda's breathing in the dark deepens, finding a more measured rhythm. It seems she is finally calming down.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: To be honest, I don't know how to answer you. I'm not even sure if what we're doing is right or wrong.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We can only move forward until history renders its final judgment on us.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...It wasn't... like this before.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I still remember when I was young, hearing about the future, from books, from my parents, from the news. Everyone said the future would be an ideal era.
She narrows her eyes, as if admiring the dust motes dancing in the darkness.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Ever since the Nightfall, the metropoles have united settlements and city-states, providing aid for decades.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I once saw towns on the brink of extinction rebuilt with the metropoles' help. Refugees fleeing from catastrophes would embrace each other in tears when they finally reached our gates...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That same year, Sevael proclaimed to all territories that if every city-state united and contributed what it could, even the greatest disasters could be overcome.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Small states are not burdens, but our flesh and blood. Resources are not barriers, but bridges between us... If we stand united, civilization's light will burn away the long night, and humanity... will rise again.
She raises her hand, reaching for a memory, a ghost—for something that was never there. At last, it falls back to her side, empty.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, I believe the evidence we've seen, but I can't dismiss everything the metropoles have done for decades because of a few isolated cases.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Maybe we've missed something, or something's been hidden from us... The information we don't have might explain everything.
You open your mouth, but find you have no words to offer.

You understand that these recent revelations are feeble things against the fortress of her faith, a devotion built over decades. Beginnings are always pure; memories are forever gilded. You cannot fault her for clinging to the memory of those idealistic orators and a metropole that once truly reached out to help the smaller states.
To press further now would only seed suspicion. For today, it is wiser to let the matter rest.

steps.speaker: Option
options: I was thinking the same thing.

steps.content: Hilda draws a deep, steadying breath, the ghost of a smile touching her lips.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: If the mole brought me this information, they must know even more than I do.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I... won't be shaken by this. Even if it's just to learn the whole truth, I'll find that mole and make them talk.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I need to know what kind of "justice" they claim to uphold while sending so many people to kill me...
Hilda rises slowly and walks through the dim light. She passes you, her form dissolving into a darkness that seems to promise no return.

In her silhouette, you see the ghosts of others you have known. They always begin this way—eyes clear, stride steady, ideals held like a shield, heads high against the sky. And so often, they end this way, too—stepping onto a solitary path, from which there is no coming back.
[Main Hall]
Amidst the devastation of the main hall, the survivors have assembled. Helene, having foraged for food and ignited a surviving stove, now beckons the others toward the comforting circle of fire.

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: Look... I have a suggestion. Instead of splitting into shifts tonight, why don't we all just stay here together?

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: So we can all keep a closer eye on one another, you mean?

steps.speaker: Helene
steps.content: I mean we can protect one another! The situation is still unclear. Staying in a group is the most logical way to ensure everyone's safety. It's obvious!
Nolaine lets out a cold snort.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: Hmph, a group is just a bigger target. I have no intention of dozing off only to have my throat slit by the person sharing my fire. Separately, we stay sharp. That's how you survive.

steps.speaker: Nolaine
steps.content: And with today's chaos, the Monolith research can't be finished. I assume Hilda would prefer some quiet to work.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The location is irrelevant to me.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The Monolith's repairs are almost done; I can work from anywhere. Our priority now should be determining which arrangement is more likely to... flush out the remaining "mole."
Hilda's voice is a soft veil over steel, her words needling straight into the hearts of everyone present.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Perhaps we should put it to a vote? Look, there are exactly five of us.
Right now, the vote is locked, two against two. As the fifth and final vote, the decision is yours alone—
